description: Ignore everything after the first 1 bits: those leading bits must be 0. Use a binary alphabet.
A binary word passes only when 0 is right at its left edge; a later occurrence does not count.
Read a sequence of bits and accept it precisely when its trailing block is 0.
For binary input, require 0 at the right edge. Nothing earlier in the word matters.
In a bit sequence, find 0 as one uninterrupted run somewhere; accept exactly when it occurs.
The binary pattern 0 has to occur at least once, possibly overlapping another occurrence.
Even one occurrence of 0 disqualifies a bit sequence. Otherwise accept it.
A binary word is allowed only if the consecutive pattern 0 never appears, including across repeated overlaps.
